title: Applied Digital vs. IREN: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Sara Appino
description: The article compares two AI infrastructure companies: Applied Digital (APLD) and IREN (IREN). Applied Digital shows stronger margins (22.38% vs 9.84%) and lower P/S ratio (13.1x vs 23.0x) but faces customer concentration risk with CoreWeave. IREN has secured major contracts with Microsoft ($9.7B) and Nvidia ($3.4B) and is pivoting from crypto mining to AI cloud services, though it reported a massive net loss of $702.6M. The author recommends IREN for patient investors due to its stronger contracted revenue base and blue-chip customer relationships, despite both companies currently losing money.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company shows strong revenue growth (183.7% YoY) and superior gross margins (22.38%), but faces significant customer concentration risk with CoreWeave, high debt-to-equity ratio (2.9x), and substantial net losses (-39.9% margin). Positive operational metrics offset by structural risks.

Despite massive net losses (-99.4% margin) and high debt ($7.98B), IREN has secured substantial long-term contracts with Microsoft ($9.7B) and Nvidia ($3.4B), providing revenue visibility. Nvidia's certification as reference-quality provider and successful pivot from crypto mining to AI infrastructure are significant positives. Author's recommendation favors this company.
Mentioned as Applied Digital's primary customer with full contract of flagship Polaris Forge 1 site, representing both revenue opportunity and concentration risk for APLD.
Mentioned as major customer of IREN with $9.7B five-year contract, indicating confidence in IREN's infrastructure capabilities.
Mentioned as IREN customer ($3.4B contract) and hardware supplier to both companies; certified IREN as reference-quality cloud provider, validating operational competence.

title: CoreWeave vs. QuantumScape: Which Stock Is a Better Investment, the AI Giant or the EV Battery Upstart?
author: Robert Izquierdo
description: CoreWeave, an AI data center provider, and QuantumScape, a pre-revenue solid-state battery developer, represent different high-risk technology bets. CoreWeave shows impressive 167.9% revenue growth to $5.1B but carries heavy debt (8.9x debt-to-equity) and customer concentration risk with Microsoft accounting for 67% of revenue. QuantumScape has a strong balance sheet (0.1x debt-to-equity) but remains pre-commercial with no revenue until at least 2029. The author recommends CoreWeave as the safer bet due to its immediate revenue growth and multi-year AI infrastructure demand runway.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong 167.9% YoY revenue growth ($5.1B in FY2025), impressive Q2 sales of $2.6B with 112% YoY growth, and forecasted $12.4B revenue for 2026. Benefits from sustained AI infrastructure demand. However, sentiment is tempered by high debt levels (8.9x debt-to-equity), negative free cash flow (-$7.3B), and heavy Microsoft customer concentration (67% of revenue).

Strong balance sheet fundamentals (0.1x debt-to-equity, 15.9x current ratio) and strategic partnerships with Volkswagen and Honda provide long-term potential. However, pre-revenue status, no commercial product until 2029, and negative free cash flow (-$278.8M) create significant uncertainty. High-risk, long-term bet with execution risk.
Mentioned as CoreWeave's primary customer (67% of revenue), indicating strong AI infrastructure demand but also representing concentration risk for CoreWeave's business model.
Mentioned as a CoreWeave client through multi-year agreements for AI compute capacity, indicating demand for specialized AI infrastructure services.
Identified as a limited hardware supplier to CoreWeave, creating supply chain vulnerability and dependency risk.
Entered multi-year development partnership with QuantumScape in mid-2026, expanding QuantumScape's commercialization opportunities but still pre-revenue.
Strategic partner with QuantumScape for solid-state battery commercialization through PowerCo subsidiary, critical to QuantumScape's success but also represents dependency risk.

title: SpaceX's First 100 Days Are in the Books. Here's the Report Card.
author: Jeremy Bowman
description: SpaceX has completed its first 100 days as a public company, trading near its IPO price of $150 after an initial surge and 50% decline. The company has dramatically accelerated revenue growth to 92% in Q2 through AI compute rental deals with Anthropic and Google, with segment adjusted EBITDA nearly tripling. While investor sentiment has stabilized through lockup expirations, SpaceX's $2.1 trillion valuation appears expensive compared to peers like Meta, and the company remains unprofitable on a GAAP basis despite strong EBITDA performance.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While SpaceX shows impressive Q2 revenue acceleration (92%) and strong EBITDA growth driven by AI compute deals, the company remains unprofitable on GAAP basis with a $541M Q2 loss. At $2.1T market cap, valuation appears stretched compared to peers like Meta, and AI rental revenue may not be a long-term growth driver. Stock has stabilized but lacks compelling value proposition relative to alternatives.

Meta is highlighted as a more attractive investment alternative to SpaceX, offering lower market cap, high growth, wide margins, and reasonable valuation. The article suggests Meta is a better buy than SpaceX for investors seeking quality growth at fair prices.
Google signed a significant AI compute rental agreement with SpaceX, contributing to the company's 92% Q2 revenue growth and validating demand for SpaceX's AI infrastructure capabilities.

title: IREN Broadens Its AI Customer Base: Can Diversification Pay Off?
author: Na
description: IREN Limited is diversifying its AI cloud customer base away from heavy dependence on Microsoft and NVIDIA by signing $2.8 billion in contracts with Prometheus, Perplexity, and Together AI in July 2026. The company is experiencing stronger contract economics with three-year pricing up 125% and five-year pricing up 70%, though it faces risks from early-stage customers and shorter contracts. With 2026 capacity largely sold out, IREN is targeting broader customer expansion for 2027-2028.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company signed significant $2.8B in new contracts, achieved substantial pricing increases (125% for 3-year, 70% for 5-year contracts), and is successfully diversifying customer base away from concentration risk. However, sentiment is tempered by downward earnings revisions and premium valuation.

Strong Q2 2026 performance with $2.58B in revenues and $104B revenue backlog. Demonstrates significant scale with 1.5 GW active power and 3.7 GW contracted power, positioning it well in the competitive AI cloud market.
Solid Q2 2026 results with $582.3M group revenues and $3B ARR. Closed four major AI-cloud deals averaging over $1B each and raised contracted-power target to 5 GW, indicating strong growth momentum.

title: Down 53%, Should You Still Buy CoreWeave's (CRWV) Stock?
author: Leo Sun
description: CoreWeave's stock has declined 53% from its June 2025 peak of $183.58 to $86, but the article argues it may represent a buying opportunity. The AI infrastructure provider operates 51 data centers with over 250,000 Nvidia GPUs, serving major clients like Meta, Microsoft, and OpenAI. Despite explosive 168% revenue growth to $5.1B in 2025 and a $104B contracted revenue backlog, CoreWeave remains unprofitable under GAAP accounting with a concerning 14.3 debt-to-equity ratio. Analysts project continued strong growth through 2028, valuing the stock at just 12x adjusted EBITDA.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite 53% stock decline, the article presents a bullish case citing strong revenue growth (168%), massive contracted backlog ($104B), competitive advantages (35x faster, 80% cheaper than AWS/Azure), and attractive valuation (12x adjusted EBITDA). Positioned as a 'compelling turnaround play' with 101-110% projected CAGR through 2028.

Nvidia benefits from CoreWeave's expansion as the primary GPU supplier with 250,000+ GPUs installed. Nvidia's 11.5% stake in CoreWeave and strategic partnership position it favorably in the AI infrastructure boom.
Mentioned as a top CoreWeave customer, indicating reliance on AI infrastructure services, but no specific sentiment drivers regarding Meta itself are discussed in the article.
